title: Piceatannol protects against sepsis-induced myocardial dysfunction via direct inhibition of JAK2.
authors: Xie, Lingpeng; Wu, Yuting; Zhou, Chuying; Tan, Zhangbin; Xu, Honglin; Chen, Guanghong; Chen, Hongmei; Huang, Guiqiong; Fan, Huijie; Gao, Lei; Liu, Bin; Zhou, Yingchun
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨白皮杉醇通过抑制JAK2蛋白改善脓毒症心肌功能障碍，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sepsis-induced myocardial dysfunction (SIMD) represents one of the serious complications secondary to sepsis, which is a leading cause of the high mortality rate among septic cases. Subsequent cardiomyocyte apoptosis, together with the uncontrolled inflammatory response, has been suggested to be closely related to SIMD. Piceatannol (PIC) is verified with potent anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory effects, but its function and molecular mechanism in SIMD remain unknown so far. This study aimed to explore the potential role and mechanism of action of PIC in resisting SIMD. The interaction of PIC with JAK2 proteins was evaluated by molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and surface plasmon resonance imaging (SPRi). The cecal ligation and puncture-induced septicemia mice and the LPS-stimulated H9C2 cardiomyocytes were prepared as the models in vivo and in vitro, separately. Molecular docking showed that JAK2-PIC complex had the -8.279 kcal/mol binding energy. MD simulations showed that JAK2-PIC binding was stable. SPRi analysis also showed that PIC has a strong binding affinity to JAK2. PIC treatment significantly ameliorated the cardiac function, attenuated the sepsis-induced myocardial loss, and suppressed the myocardial inflammatory responses both in vivo and in vitro. Further detection revealed that PIC inhibited the activation of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling, which was tightly associated with apoptosis and inflammation. Importantly, pre-incubation with a JAK2 inhibitor (AG490) partially blocked the cardioprotective effects of PIC. Collectively, the findings demonstrated that PIC restored the impaired cardiac function by attenuating the sepsis-induced apoptosis and inflammation via suppressing the JAK2/STAT3 pathway both in septic mice and H9C2 cardiomyocytes.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症诱导的心肌功能障碍（SIMD）是脓毒症的严重并发症之一，也是导致脓毒症患者高死亡率的主要原因。随后的心肌细胞凋亡以及失控的炎症反应被认为与SIMD密切相关。白皮杉醇（PIC）已被证实具有强效的抗凋亡和抗炎作用，但其在SIMD中的功能及分子机制至今尚不清楚。本研究旨在探讨PIC抵抗SIMD的潜在作用及其作用机制。通过分子对接、分子动力学（MD）模拟和表面等离子体共振成像（SPRi）评估PIC与JAK2蛋白的相互作用。分别制备盲肠结扎穿刺诱导的脓毒症小鼠和脂多糖（LPS）刺激的H9C2心肌细胞作为体内和体外模型。分子对接显示，JAK2-PIC复合物的结合能为-8.279 kcal/mol。MD模拟表明JAK2-PIC结合稳定。SPRi分析也显示PIC对JAK2具有强结合亲和力。PIC处理显著改善了心脏功能，减轻了脓毒症诱导的心肌损失，并在体内和体外抑制了心肌炎症反应。进一步检测发现，PIC抑制了JAK2/STAT3信号通路的激活，该通路与凋亡和炎症密切相关。重要的是，预先孵育JAK2抑制剂（AG490）部分阻断了PIC的心脏保护作用。综上所述，研究结果表明，PIC通过抑制JAK2/STAT3通路，减轻脓毒症诱导的凋亡和炎症，从而恢复受损的心脏功能，这一作用在脓毒症小鼠和H9C2心肌细胞中均得到验证。
